title: Max your HSA if eligible
summary: Triple-tax-advantaged. Even more valuable for self-employed than W-2 because your tax burden is higher.
detailsHtml:
The HSA reduces both income tax and self-employment tax (when the HSA contribution is made through an employer cafeteria plan — for sole proprietors, contributions reduce income tax but not SE tax). For a contractor in the 24% federal + 15.3% SE + 5% state bracket, an HSA contribution saves ~44 cents per dollar if structured through an S-corp; ~29 cents per dollar as a sole proprietor.

2026 HSA limits unchanged from W-2 path: $4,400 self-only $8,750 family +$1,000 catch-up at 55+
